claim:as-forage-and-survival.proposition: The agent forages both resources in 12 of 16 FAR, high-drain environments (sep 42-62, asymmetric per-nutrient drain) and is STATE-DEPENDENT: it uses its internal nutrient sensors to prioritize the faster-draining resource (ablating them costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both), rather than the blind circling of the earlier regime.

claim:as-switching-dynamics.proposition: Distance to A and B are anti-phase and the nutrients sawtooth in step with engagement — the agent rhythmically switches between foraging the two resources.

claim:as-morphology-comparison.proposition: The three morphologies differ in chemosensor placement and whether they have internal nutrient sensors; the evolved, analyzed agent is morphology M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors).

narrative.question:
Can a single CTRNN agent with internal metabolic state autonomously switch
between two foraging actions — approaching two different chemical resources to
keep two nutrient levels alive — purely through the dynamics of its coupled
brain-body-environment system, with no higher-level action-selection
mechanism?

decisions.title: Report the M2 agent as the single analyzed agent (as the paper does), or also evolve M1/M3 for a full morphology comparison?
decisions.detail: The paper's deep dynamical analysis is of ONE morphology-2 agent. M1/M3 are presented here structurally; evolving them is a documented extension.
